changes.after: HTML uses special characters such as a less-than sign to mark up a page. Escape text so those characters can be shown literally.

before: htmlspecialchars converts HTML-significant characters for HTML text and suitably quoted attribute values. The bitwise | operator combines flag bits; it is not logical ||. ENT_QUOTES escapes both quote kinds; ENT_SUBSTITUTE replaces invalid encoding sequences, and UTF-8 states the intended encoding. This is output encoding, not general input validation.

The result here is a String verified in CLI, not a rendered browser security test. JavaScript, CSS and URL contexts have different rules. Escaping an attribute does not make a dangerous URL scheme safe; choose and validate the destination context separately.
Expected output or behavior: <b>"read"</b>. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

after.question: What does escaping A&B produce?
after.explanation: An ampersand itself must be written as & in this HTML text.
